Pulling goes first on upper days, because almost everyone already has more pressing volume than pulling - and whatever you do first gets your best effort.

Training fasted doesn't burn more fat over a day. You burn slightly more during the session and slightly less afterwards. It evens out. That's it. What actually decides fat loss: total energy across the week, protein high enough to hold muscle, and doing it long enough to count. Train fasted if you prefer it - just don't expect a bonus.

There's no such thing as perfect form. There's form that suits you. Limb lengths you can't change. Ankle and hip mobility. What you're actually trying to load. Copying someone else's squat because it looks right is how people get hurt. Good form is repeatable, controlled, and doesn't hurt. If something IS painful, get it looked at properly - that's not a programming problem.
